entries.summary: DaemonConfig.runtimes.grok takes compatInstructions, agentUserMcpServers and versionPolicy, and createDaemon builds the Grok adapter from configuration when runtimeAllowlist lists grok (#1094). Without grok in the allowlist nothing changes; a Host that assembles GrokAdapter itself can move those options into DaemonConfig.

The embedded server's SQLite file is now schema 8 (#1113 A2b): the activity log is persisted in the database instead of process memory, so task activity and its cursors survive a restart, and the terminal-task archive removes it in its own transaction. A schema 6 or 7 file is upgraded in place when it opens, inside the open transaction, keeping its pairings, tasks, approvals and other rows; 7 to 8 adds activity_log_head and activity_log_entry empty, since no activity history was persisted before. The upgrade is one-way: 0.32.0 and earlier refuse a schema 8 file, so stop the server and back up the database file before the first open with this release. Schema 8 also closes a task's activity log and approval timeline in the same transaction as its first terminal or accepted Host cancellation (#1113 A3); the 7 to 8 upgrade rebuilds approval_timeline_tail without the idle deadline, keeping every observation, and closes already-closed tasks at their original deadline. A v8 file missing either activity table or the closure trigger is refused as SQLITE_SCHEMA_INVALID.

An approval timeline no longer idle-expires (#1113 A3). It closes in the same transaction as its task's first terminal or accepted Host cancellation and expires ten minutes after that instant; reads and replays never renew it. ApprovalTimelineAppendInput loses ttlMs, and ApprovalTimelineTail gains terminalAt while its expiresAt becomes optional, present only once closed. On a closed timeline ApprovalTimelineStore.append throws the new approval_timeline_settled code and resolvePending returns absent, so a request pending at the close can no longer be decided; ByokCloud refuses a late task.await_approval with task_settled_by_cloud. A timeline keeps at most 50 observations and MAX_APPROVAL_TIMELINE_BYTES (1 MiB) of serialized observations, evicting the oldest first and never the pending request; one event is at most MAX_APPROVAL_EVENT_BYTES and capacity must be 2 to 50, else coordination_input_invalid. Archive, redaction and expiry clear a closed timeline's entries and keep its row as the fence. A custom ApprovalTimelineStore must close with its task, refuse appends once closed, and retain through retainApprovalObservations or the same bounds; pendingApprovalObservation is the shared pending fold.

A task's activity log and approval timeline close in the same transaction as its first terminal or accepted Host cancellation, in every built-in composition (#1113 A3). Later task.progress, task.artifact and task.await_approval are refused with task_settled_by_cloud, also on a redacted or archived task, and both expire ten minutes after the closing instant without renewal. CLOUD_ERROR_CODES gains approval_timeline_settled. The in-memory InMemoryTaskAttemptStore, InMemoryTaskCancellationStore and InMemoryDeviceDirectory close them through the attempt state, and a custom composition must close both in the same commit as its first terminal or accepted cancellation. Postgres migration 0035 adds the closing trigger on task and approval_timeline_tail.terminal_at with a constraint that only a closed row has expires_at, drops the idle deadline of every open timeline, and closes already-closed tasks at their original deadline. Deploy 0035 and the code together: each fails against the other's approval schema. Apply 0035 only through deploy/scripts/migrate, and on a large tenant in a maintenance window: it scans task and rewrites approval_timeline_tail in one transaction that blocks writes to task.

A content-free task events wake (#1113 A4): TaskEventsWake hints that a task's state, activity log or approval timeline changed, naming only the tenant and task, so a reader re-reads those sources instead of polling. createInMemoryCloudStores and the embedded SQLite composition expose taskEventsWake, which every write to those stores signals after it commits; a rollback signals nothing. createPostgresTaskEventsWake listens on a session-mode DSN for the triggers migration 0036 adds on task, activity_log_head and approval_timeline_tail (additive; either deployment order is safe, and code before 0036 reads at its fallback interval), so commits on any instance, maintenance included, wake readers on every instance. A lost hint delays a reader by at most fallbackMs (DEFAULT_TASK_EVENTS_WAKE_FALLBACK_MS, 5 seconds) and a listener reconnect wakes every subscription. createInProcessTaskEventsWake covers writers in one process only. The Postgres listener options are now the shared PostgresWakeOptions, which PostgresMailboxWakeOptions names unchanged.

ByokServer.tasks.events and TaskHandle.events() read the durable activity log, task state and the approval timeline instead of an in-process relay buffer (#1113). Cursors resume across a restart over the same SQLite file, including inside a progress batch; cursors from 0.32.0 and earlier are refused as TaskEventsUnavailableError cursor_unknown. State is the current fact, coalesced, not a replay of every transition. A terminal task stays readable while its activity is retained, so the feed_expired reason is gone; events_truncated now marks activity the log dropped before the reader reached it, also for a cursor taken before the task had any activity. Readers wait on the stores' task events wake, with its five-second fallback. CreateByokServerOptions.taskEventBufferLimit and taskEventRetentionMs and the DEFAULT_TASK_EVENT_BUFFER_LIMIT and DEFAULT_TASK_EVENT_RETENTION_MS exports are removed. events.subscribe() announces task.state only for tasks this instance dispatched.

Add DshAdapter, a DeepSeek Harness (dsh) runtime adapter over ACP (`dsh --profile acp`) reached by the custom harness id dsh (#1258). The Host constructs it with an SDK-owned persistent home that is not ~/.dsh and a provider, model and keyEnv selection; it resumes native sessions, attaches task MCP toolsets including result documents, declines auto and file-scope tasks before claim, and runs on darwin and linux. fakeRuntimeAdapter accepts 'dsh'. Nothing changes for a Host that does not construct it.

RuntimeAdapterDescriptor gains optional fileScope ({ lanes }) and providerProfileBinding, and RuntimeAdapter gains an optional projectMcpEnvironment(env). The daemon reads these declarations for file-scope admission, the provider-profile-binding capability and the MCP environment of probes and task MCP servers, instead of checking for the runtime id pi. PiAdapter declares all three, so built-in behavior is unchanged. A custom adapter needs no change; one that reused the id pi without enforcing a file scope no longer admits scoped offers until it declares fileScope.
